You fitted the model as a structural equation model with lavaan and want the
same effects and tables. Part of the [Models](models.html) collection.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Structure** | simple, serial or parallel mediation, written as lavaan syntax |
| **Class returned** | `MediationData`, `SerialMediationData` or `ParallelMediationData` |
| **Route** | `extract_mediation(<lavaan fit>, treatment = , mediator = , outcome = )` |
| **Needs** | `lavaan` |

```{r}
#| label: setup
library(medfit)
library(generics)
has_lavaan <- requireNamespace("lavaan", quietly = TRUE)
covs <- "covariate1 + covariate2"
```

## Simple mediation

Label the paths in the syntax, fit with `lavaan::sem()`, then extract:

```{r}
#| label: simple
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
syntax <- paste0("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + ", covs, "
  outcome ~ b * mediator1 + c_prime * treatment + ", covs)
fit <- lavaan::sem(syntax, data = mediation_demo)
x <- extract_mediation(fit, treatment = "treatment", mediator = "mediator1",
                       outcome = "outcome")
class(x)[1]
tidy(x, type = "effects", conf.int = TRUE)
```

Every function from the [simple mediation page](model-simple.html) works on `x`.

## Serial mediation

Give `mediator` two names, in chain order. The class follows the structure:

```{r}
#| label: serial
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
syntax_s <- paste0("
  mediator1 ~ a * treatment + ", covs, "
  mediator2 ~ d * mediator1 + a2 * treatment + ", covs, "
  outcome ~ b * mediator2 + b1 * mediator1 + c_prime * treatment + ", covs)
xs <- extract_mediation(lavaan::sem(syntax_s, data = mediation_demo),
                        treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator2"),
                        outcome = "outcome")
class(xs)[1]
tidy(xs, type = "effects", conf.int = TRUE)
```

The row `nie` is the chain through both mediators; `nie_total` adds the paths that
skip a mediator. See [Serial mediation](model-serial.html).

## Parallel mediation

```{r}
#| label: parallel
#| eval: !expr has_lavaan
syntax_p <- paste0("
  mediator1 ~ a1 * treatment + ", covs, "
  mediator3 ~ a2 * treatment + ", covs, "
  outcome ~ b1 * mediator1 + b2 * mediator3 + c_prime * treatment + ", covs)
xp <- extract_mediation(lavaan::sem(syntax_p, data = mediation_demo),
                        treatment = "treatment",
                        mediator = c("mediator1", "mediator3"),
                        outcome = "outcome", structure = "parallel")
class(xp)[1]
nie(xp)
```

## Why use a lavaan fit

The equations are fitted together, so the stored covariance includes the
covariances among the paths. That matters most for serial chains, where the
lm/glm route sets them to zero (see [Serial mediation](model-serial.html)).

## Limits

- **The regressions must name the variables.** `extract_mediation()` finds each
  path by the variable names, so the model must contain `outcome ~ mediator1`;
  if it does not, extraction stops with "Could not find b path (mediator ->
  outcome)".
- **Four-way effects** (a treatment-by-mediator product) need the mean structure
  and a specific syntax; see [Model Extraction](extraction.html) for what is
  supported before relying on it.
- To write a model as syntax **without** lavaan, with latent mediators and
  constraints, use the [native engine](model-native.html).
